rows.grounds: Bahuvrīhi compound specifying measures: ṣaṭ (six), catur (four), dvi (two), aṅgula (finger-unit).
Compound of āyāma (length), vistāra (breadth), and unnati (height/elevation).
Adjective qualifying the ritual fire-pit (kuṇḍa) as possessing the stated dimensions.

items.question: What specific length, breadth, and height measurements must the ritual fire-pit possess?
premises: The ritual fire-pit requires defined dimensional proportions.
The measures are specified in finger-units as six, four, and two.
These measures correspond respectively to length, breadth, and height.
items.inference: The properly constructed ritual fire-pit must possess a length of six finger-units, a breadth of four finger-units, and a height of two finger-units.
uncertainties: The exact order of mapping six, four, and two to length, breadth, and height follows traditional convention but is not explicitly marked by case relations in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: The ritual fire-pit should have a length of six finger-units, a breadth of four finger-units, and a height of two finger-units.
